  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that a person who sins is worse than the nations of the world in their essential state, who naturally recognize the God of gods.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">What is written in the maamar "Bati LeGani" 5713, at the end of the section,</t>
    <t s="1">that "the nations of the world and the klipot and the sitra achra do not transgress His will... </t>
    <t s="2">and a person who commits a transgression, rebelling against His will, is worse, etc." – its explanation is,</t>
    <t s="3">that one who commits a transgression is worse than the nations of the world as they are essentially, in their own right</t>
    <t s="4">(before they do anything),</t>
    <t s="5">and this means,</t>
    <t s="6">that by the nature of creation, there must always be within them the recognition of "the God of gods,"</t>
    <t s="7">so that then they would not be able to transgress His will,</t>
    <t s="8">as per the statement of Bilaam, "I cannot transgress the word of G-d";</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that nevertheless, through the spirit of folly, the nations of the world can choose to transgress the Seven Noachide Laws.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">But certainly, regarding the matter of free choice, the nations of the world can also follow the spirit of folly and transgress the Seven Noachide Laws,</t>
    <t s="1">as with Bilaam,</t>
    <t s="2">that through the spirit of folly which covers and conceals,</t>
    <t s="3">there was within him the matter of "I have ventured"</t>
    <t s="4">(</t>
    <t s="5">Sanhedrin 102,</t>
    <t s="6">b)</t>
    <t s="7">,</t>
    <t s="8">b)</t>

    <t s="10">which is one of the Seven Noachide Laws.</t>
  </section>

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section is an addition to the maamar.
This section explains that a person who sins is worse than the nations of the world in their essential state, who naturally recognize the God of gods.

translations.translation: What is written in the maamar "Bati LeGani" 5713, at the end of the section,
that "the nations of the world and the klipot and the sitra achra do not transgress His will...
and a person who commits a transgression, rebelling against His will, is worse, etc." – its explanation is,
that one who commits a transgression is worse than the nations of the world as they are essentially, in their own right
that by the nature of creation, there must always be within them the recognition of "the God of gods,"
so that then they would not be able to transgress His will,
as per the statement of Bilaam, "I cannot transgress the word of G-d";

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that nevertheless, through the spirit of folly, the nations of the world can choose to transgress the Seven Noachide Laws.

translations.translation: But certainly, regarding the matter of free choice, the nations of the world can also follow the spirit of folly and transgress the Seven Noachide Laws,
that through the spirit of folly which covers and conceals,
there was within him the matter of "I have ventured"
which is one of the Seven Noachide Laws.
